opener_episode.title: Episode 516 w/ Mistah F.A.B.
opener_episode.why: Most recent new interview, and its theme (independent hustle from the streets to a recognized brand and entrepreneur) mirrors Avery's story of taking street artist Alec Monopoly from street work to sold-out shows and brand partnerships. Alternative: Ep. 515 (hip-hop media) if pitching the culture-documentation angle.

angles.headline: From the streets to the gallery: how a graffiti artist became a global brand
angles.pitch: The Miami dealer who developed street artist Alec Monopoly into a global brand (sold-out shows from New York to Morocco, major brand partnerships) breaks down how street culture goes blue-chip.
angles.builds_on: Ep. 516 Mistah F.A.B. (independent hustle to brand)

angles.headline: What the stars actually buy: celebrity art stories from Art Basel
angles.pitch: Avery advises celebrities and athletes on art; he placed a $100K+ Hap Tivey work with Kris Jenner at Art Basel Miami Beach 2024 and sold Scott Disick a $57K Helmut Newton print, and can tell the fame-money-outlandish-request stories the show thrives on.
angles.builds_on: The show's celebrity-storytelling format; Miami Art Week (Art Basel Miami Beach Dec 2026) and prior Drink Champs Wynwood/Art Week appearances

angles.headline: Backing Black artists before the market did
angles.pitch: Avery was an early champion of Hebru Brantley and Jammie Holmes, a culture-first story about spotting talent early that fits a show built on honoring legends.
angles.builds_on: Legacy/culture-honoring episodes like Ep. 514 Inspectah Deck and Ep. 515 (hip-hop media)

format: In-person, video (YouTube/REVOLT history) plus audio on iHeart. Filmed in a working bar in Miami's art district (show's own X post, 2022; current studio unverified). Long, drink-fueled, free-wheeling episodes (often 2+ hours, unverified for current eps). Weekly new episode plus throwback re-releases. Guests are overwhelmingly hip-hop artists, DJs, label execs and comedians, often from the hosts' NY/Miami networks.
red_flags: No art-world or dealer guest found; Avery is not a hip-hop name, so a pairing with a hip-hop collector/client or an Art Week tie-in raises odds. Rowdy, unscripted format (hosts have made headline-grabbing comments). Throwback re-releases fill some weeks. Booking email unverified.
